problem_statement: AzureChatOpenAI creates a new connection pool per instance instead of reusing a shared default httpx client the way BaseChatOpenAI does, wasting connection resources in high-instance-count deployments.
target_user: Backend engineers running many short-lived AzureChatOpenAI instances in a request-scoped service.

user_stories.action: have AzureChatOpenAI reuse the shared default httpx client
user_stories.value: I avoid per-instance connection pool churn and reduce resource usage under load

acceptance_criteria.given: multiple AzureChatOpenAI instances created without an explicit client
acceptance_criteria.then: they share a single default httpx connection pool rather than each creating its own

acceptance_criteria.given: an AzureChatOpenAI instance created with an explicit custom client
acceptance_criteria.then: the explicit client is used and no shared default is substituted
observable request behavior is unchanged aside from reduced pool creation

success_metrics.name: connection pool count under load
success_metrics.definition: number of distinct httpx connection pools created during a fixed high-instance benchmark
success_metrics.target: reduced to a single shared pool for the default path

risks.description: Sharing a default pool across instances could couple their lifecycles in ways that surprise users who assumed isolation
